newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Sales increase in Kansas.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Sales increase in Kansas.

text.p: Sales of hard red winter wheat were up sharply Thursday, Kansas grain merchandisers said Friday.

"We saw pretty decent movement yesterday. I don't know what prompted it," said a merchandiser at a terminal elevator in south central Kansas. "Among other things, we bought one round lot -- 100,000 bushels -- from one elevator."
Dealers speculated that farmers had sold wheat to local elevators in response to Thursday's climb in KCBT March wheat futures, and that the elevators, in turn, had decided to sell wheat to terminals.
Another dealer in central Kansas said his firm bought 50,000 bushels of wheat after the market closed.
But merchandisers in Oklahoma reported another slow day of sales.
Basis levels for hard red winter wheat early Friday were steady to lower, with most of the weakness showing up in Kansas bids.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: H=KCBT March wheat futures. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
